19: Ordinary address now uses you/your. Lot addresses the visitors plurally in 19:2, but his petition in 19:18–19 is singular; lord remains lower-case because the addressee’s identity is not decided by capitalization. The plural they were troubled in 19:16 and the repeated hand/hands remain.

Surrounded, do not act wickedly, and did not know replace obsolete forms. Great righteousness in 19:19 expresses the magnified righteousness of the earlier wording. The face expression in 19:21, the repeated Lord in 19:24, the account’s sexual violence and incest, and the naming explanations remain. Lot’s proposal is his speech, without editorial endorsement.
20: Abimelech’s direct address to God retains wilt Thou in 20:4. God’s address to Abimelech, and ordinary human address, use you/your. You are to die in 20:3 expresses the warning in context; it does not diagnose an ongoing illness.

Righteousness of hands, this righteousness, honour of your face, the women with Sarah, the thousand didrachms, and wholly shut every womb from outside remain. Sarah’s identity and the speakers’ explanations are not harmonized with another account.
21: Sarah is nursing in 21:7 makes the present activity natural in speech. The child’s crying and weeping, living water, the fir tree, the shoulder clause, and the two repetitions of sitting opposite him remain. The compressed shoulder clause still needs specialist review.

The oath conversation uses ordinary singular address. Plural loaves and wells, Ahuzzath the groomsman, the seven ewe lambs, the future you shall take, and Abraham’s planting a field remain. Well of Swearing and Well of the Oath retain the source’s separate naming expressions.
22: Ordinary address uses you/your. The instruction to the servants in 22:5 is plural; the return includes Abraham and the lad. The angel’s my in 22:12 remains lower-case, while the explicitly attributed divine speech in 22:16 retains My/Myself.

The Lord Has Seen updates hath within the translated place name without changing its seeing verb. Beloved, high land, sheep, sabek plant, the female donkey, bound feet, slaughter, cities, and the two repetitions of Abraham’s name remain. The plant’s identity is not newly established.
23: The negotiation uses ordinary you/your: Abraham addresses the sons of Heth plurally, while the replies to Abraham and the exchange with Ephron address one person. The two status terms resident foreigner and sojourner remain; the latter describes temporary residence.

Natural clause order clarifies the giving and purchase statements. King from God, double cave, four hundred didrachms, face, ears, field, trees, borders and public witnesses remain. The repeated acquisition statements have not been shortened.
24: The prayer and its retelling retain Thou/Thy for God in 24:14, 42 and 44; the quoted requests to Rebekah use ordinary your. The family address in 24:49 is plural. The singular reply I will go and the imperative blessing become thousands of ten thousands remain.

The account and its retelling remain separate in full. Curse and oath, the thigh, the virgin/maiden distinction, the water jar, earrings and their weights, plural brothers, possessions, cities, and the mother’s house remain. Speaking in his mind has not been recast as an audible prayer.
25: Without pretence in 25:27 makes the inherited unfeigned intelligible. It is a provisional contextual rendering of aplastos, not a claim that Jacob never deceived anyone; straightforward or unsophisticated remains a lexical-review alternative. The singular house is retained.

All genealogical entries and ages remain. Greater and lesser in 25:23 have not been replaced by older and younger. The red stew, hairy hide, held heel, birthright and repeated death formulas remain. Modern bore and begot change English verb forms, not relationships.
26: God’s address to Isaac and the individual human conversations now use you/your; Isaac’s question to the visiting group in 26:27 is plural. Natural negatives and current verb forms replace antique grammar.

Playing, unwitting offence, barley, farmland, living water, the translated well names, oath with a curse, and safety remain. The negative in We found no water at 26:32 is expressly retained. Elon remains Hivite here; chapter 36 has not been used to harmonize him.
27: Ordinary address now uses you/your. My soul may bless you, voice and hands, the repeated fragrance, dew, richness and grain/wine remain. Harran at 27:43 follows the accepted Genesis 11 place spelling. Bare parts in 27:16 remains an adjective, not the childbirth verb bore.

Isaac’s astonishment and being deeply moved remain. The rebuke and blessing retain their repetitions. Of the richness and when you cast down in 27:39–40 remain provisional; no missing object or reversed away from sense has been supplied. The sentence across 27:44–45 remains divided at its existing verse boundary.
28: God’s address to Jacob uses you/your. Jacob’s vow changes from speaking about God to directly addressing Him in 28:22; that address retains Thou givest and Thee. Harran follows the accepted place spelling.

My God, ladder, stone by his head, sand, the sea direction, House of God and Oulamlous remain. The if clause across 28:20–21 is expressed in current English. Safety remains a safe return; no architectural or doctrinal interpretation is added.
29: Questions such as Where are you from? and Do you know Laban? now use natural spoken English. Harran follows the accepted benchmark. The address to the shepherds in 29:4–7 is plural; the wage and marriage conversations chiefly address individuals.

The lifted feet, well’s mouth, repeated mother’s brother, bones and flesh, seven-year periods, week, slave women and naming speeches remain. Weak eyes and hated are retained without adding a medical diagnosis or weakening hate into a general rule of less loved.
30: The English uses current ordinary-address forms and direct sentence order. Knees, fruit of the womb, voice, mandrakes, hired, righteousness and the foot image remain. Each naming speech remains the character’s own explanation.

The difficult divination clause in 30:27 remains provisional. All animal markings, plant designations and breeding clauses remain, including the repeated coming to drink in 30:38 and unmarked/marked in 30:42. These have not been changed to the familiar weak/strong contrast. Botanical identification and interpretation still need review. The doubled exceedingly in 30:43 restores the repeated adverb visible in the declared Rahlfs–Hanhart running text; the earlier English had only one.
31: Face replaces countenance in 31:2 and 5, preserving the repeated image. The address to Rachel and Leah in 31:5–9 is plural; the subsequent quoted addresses to Jacob are singular. The ordinary-address grammar has been modernized without changing those speakers.

Ten lambs in 31:7 and ten ewe lambs in 31:41 remain; no ten times has been substituted. Idols, search order, the warning about evil, and the stated bodily condition remain. Existing numbering skips 31:51; the heap-and-pillar material is at 31:48, and Laban’s departure remains 32:1. The conditional oath in 31:50–53 still needs syntactic review.
32: Jacob’s direct prayer in 32:10–13 retains didst, Thou and Thy; the divine words quoted inside that prayer address Jacob as you/your. The instruction to the servants is plural, and the instruction to the first servant in 32:18 is singular. The chapter retains all 33 existing verse labels.

Camp/Encampments, sufficient righteousness and truth, the staff, all livestock numbers, the face expressions and Form of God remain. The wrestler remains a man with uncertain pronouns lower-case. Numbness has not been replaced by dislocation. The mother-with-children clause remains for syntactic review.
33: Ordinary address uses you/your. The repeated bows, face/face of God comparison, mercy, grace and blessings remain distinct. Possessive yours replaces thine where no following noun occurs.

Booths, Salem, a hundred lambs, and calling upon the God of Israel remain. Houses for Jacob and booths for livestock retain their different nouns. The careful pace of children and nursing animals has not been shortened.
34: Ordinary address uses you/your, with the collective negotiation addressing groups. Prostitute replaces harlot in 34:31. Household clarifies the people of Jacob’s house in 34:30. The seized/lay with/violated sequence and the massacre remain explicit.

Horite, named speakers Simeon and Levi, plural our daughters, one family, every male, captives and plunder remain. The speeches and the narrative stay distinct; no approval of assault or vengeance has been added. The old notes retain the lexical questions concerning maiden and slain.
35: Household in 35:2 clarifies the people addressed. Current tense forms and direct sentence order replace antique grammar while keeping the repeated divine naming and blessing.

The difficult destroyed them to this day in 35:4 remains. The tower sentence remains within 35:16; there is no new 35:21. Both parts of 35:22, the legacy split-label anchors, the soul-departure image, all sons and the age of Isaac remain. The chronology has not been harmonized.
36: Modern bore and lived replace the older verb forms, and the repeated succession formula now says in his place. Every genealogy, chief, king, wife, parent-child relationship and place name remains in its existing order.

The differing wife lists, Iamin, Onan/Onas, the four sons in 36:27, Arad son of Barad, and Matred as a son remain. These are retained source-history questions, not resolved readings. A specialist name-index and apparatus review is pending.
37: Natural questions and negatives replace What seek you? and saw not. Tore replaces rent in the repeated garment actions. Faces, hands, blood, tunic, pit and mourning remain concrete.

Seventeen years, eleven stars, twenty pieces of gold, Ishmaelites and Midianites, Hades, eunuch and chief cook remain. Pronouns in the selling sequence are not expanded into a new explanation. The precise aromatic substances and court titles still need specialist review.
38: Prostitute/prostitution replaces harlot/harlotry consistently with 34:31. No cultic qualification is added. Recognized distinguishes Judah’s recognition of Tamar’s pledges from knew her no more in 38:26, where the sexual idiom is retained.

Shua as Judah’s wife, Hirah as shepherd, brother-in-law duty, repeated seed, the ring/necklace/staff, and the naming explanations remain. The narrator’s account, the accusation and Judah’s comparison remain distinct. The recurring whenever in 38:9 and the scarlet-thread sequence remain.
39: Current negatives and sentence order make the account easier to hear. The two reported accusations remain distinct from each other and from the narrator’s account. The garments, hands, voice, eyes and kindled anger images remain.

Eunuch, chief cook, fortress/prison and mercy/grace retain their distinctions. Very beautiful to look at modernizes fair to behold in 39:6. Removing the redundant there after where in 39:20 clarifies English without removing either occurrence of fortress.
40: The shared night and each man’s own dream remain in 40:5, with natural sentence order. Three more days replaces in yet three days in both interpretations. The repeated office language and the contrast between remembering and forgetting remain.

Coarse bread remains a provisional lexical choice. The birds, baskets, head, flesh, tree and execution are retained without added graphic detail. Court titles retain their earlier lexical renderings and review limitations.
41: The two dreams and their retelling remain in full, including as though, seven cows, seven ears, repeated bellies and Pharaoh’s dream is one. Counting language in 41:49 makes the abundance clause natural while retaining the sand image and repeated inability to count.

The negative answer bringing deliverance in 41:16 remains provisional. Other people shave Joseph and change his clothes. The fifth, herald, hand without an added foot, Psonthomphanech, Heliopolis, ages and named sons remain. Full apparatus and lexical review are pending.
42: Recognized now expresses Joseph’s knowing his brothers while they do not recognize him. Natural questions and negatives replace obsolete forms. Address to the brothers is plural; their replies to Joseph use singular ordinary you/your.

Tracks of the country remains a provisional interpretation. Sickness, Pharaoh’s health, peaceable, affliction of his soul, required blood, silver bundles, Simeon, old age and Hades remain. The account and the brothers’ retelling have not been harmonized.
43: Stand as surety clarifies Judah’s assumption of responsibility while retaining the hand expression and lifelong guilt. Repeated questions about the father use still living. Severe expresses the growing strength of the famine, consistently with 12:10.

My God, the blessing on the father, the two nut terms, eyes, face and inward parts remain. The embodied emotion is not replaced with a new metaphor. Benjamin’s fivefold portion and became drunk remain; the narrative is not softened into merely merry.
44: The commands in 44:1–2 are plural; the subsequent instruction to the steward in 44:4 is singular. Current notes preserve this distinction despite ordinary you/your. The embedded speech in 44:5 retains my silver cup and my lord.

Divination, justified, household slaves, the care promise, sickness, soul hanging upon soul and Hades remain. Judah’s retelling retains its own details. The conditional sentence across 44:30–31 now unfolds directly, without changing whose death is feared.
45: Ordinary address uses you/your. In 45:19 the command to Joseph is singular, followed by commands to the brothers in the plural. Give this command retains the imperative. Some in carrying some of all the good things in 45:23 supplies the English partitive relation rather than claiming the donkeys carried every good thing in Egypt.

The repeated remnant, life, eyes/mouth, glory, marrow of the land, Goshen of Arabia, double robes, three hundred pieces of gold, five changes of robes and female mules remain. The rekindled spirit image remains. Do not be angry replaces be not angry.
46: Ordinary address and current verb forms make the opening vision and closing instructions natural. All genealogical entries, generation levels and stated totals remain exactly as inherited: sixty-six, nine and seventy-five have not been recalculated.

The repeated seed, Joseph’s hands upon Jacob’s eyes, plural chariots, Heroopolis, Rameses and Goshen of Arabia remain. Sara in 46:17 is the named sister in this genealogy and has not been treated as Abraham’s wife. Name-index, chronological and textual-critical reviews remain pending.
47: The repeated arrival and speech in 47:5 remain. Severe expresses the famine’s strength without changing its result. The land of the priests was the only land Joseph did not buy makes the exemption clear in natural word order.

Enslaved the people as slaves remains explicit. The fifth and four parts, bought bodies and land, seventeen years, 147 years, hand under thigh, and staff remain. The staff’s possessor is not settled by changing his. The account has not been harmonized to a relocation reading.
48: Mine and yours are used as standalone possessives. Ordinary address to Joseph is singular; in you at 48:20 is plural, the quoted blessing’s you is singular, 48:21 addresses the family plurally, and 48:22 returns to Joseph singularly.

My God, the horse-course/Chabratha wording, plural they bowed, crossed hands, both names and the repeated I know remain. Delivers in 48:16 retains present aspect. The God/angel blessing is not expanded into a doctrinal identification. The geography and blessing syntax still need specialist review.
49: The existing poetic line breaks are retained. You/your now addresses Jacob’s sons; obsolete past forms become overflowed, went up, defiled, reclined and slept. The water/boiling, soul/inward parts, lion, blood of the grape, tree, bows, breasts and womb images remain.

From a shoot, things reserved for him, joyful eyes, Joseph envied, their shattered bows and the compressed 49:24–26 remain explicitly provisional. No Shiloh, hind, fruitful bough, firm bow or spoil is imported. Both repetitions of son grown great and the repeated blessing are retained. This chapter especially requires independent lexical and syntactic review.
50: Current word order and Do not fear replace antique inversions. The repeated burial statements, forty and seventy days, seven days of mourning, Joseph’s weeping and the brothers’ fear remain.

I belong to God, God planned good, the feeding of many people, born upon Joseph’s thighs, visit/visitation, bones and coffin remain. No alternative theological question or invented ceremony is inserted. The completion of this editorial pass does not resolve the outstanding textual-critical review.
12: Ordinary address uses you/your. The addresses to Abram and Sara in this chapter are singular. Sara and Harran continue the spellings accepted in Genesis 11; the Greek has Sara here, with the name change retained in 17:15. Other names remain as inherited.

Blessed and tribes in 12:2–3, the repeated land of Canaan in 12:5, seed in 12:7, and the soul language in 12:5 and 12:13 are retained. Soul counts persons in verse 5 and refers to Abram’s life in verse 13. High oak, wilderness, calves and mules are retained; no familiar reading from another textual tradition has been substituted.

Stay in 12:10 describes Abram’s temporary residence. The stronger famine is expressed as a famine that had become severe. Pharaoh’s question in 12:19 now makes the connection between Abram’s statement and Pharaoh’s taking Sara as his wife easier to hear. The narrative’s servitude and affliction language remains explicit.
13: Ordinary address to Lot and Abram is singular and now uses you/your. Brothers in 13:8, and brother in 13:11, retain the kinship terms without changing Lot’s identity as Abram’s nephew.

The repeated inability to live together in 13:6 remains. Sand, from the east, toward the sea, lifted up his eyes, and the garden image are retained. The sea denotes the western direction without replacing the image in Scripture.

The return journey in 13:3 is expressed in ordinary English; the stated wilderness, Bethel, earlier tent site and altar remain. The supplied it in 13:4 still refers to the altar, as the earlier note explains.
14: The named kings and peoples remain as inherited. The sentence across 14:1–2 still locates the event in Amraphel’s reign and names the other kings as subjects of made war. Four kings against five remains in 14:9.

Horses in 14:11, 16 and 21, loaves in 14:18, created in 14:19 and 22, and the future I will stretch out my hand in 14:22 follow the consulted Rahlfs–Hanhart running text. These have not been harmonized to another textual tradition. The man from beyond and Lot his brother are retained, with their explanations in the earlier notes.

Address to Abram and to the king of Sodom is singular and uses you/your. In 14:20 the pronouns in he gave him remain unexpanded. The unspoken penalty of the oath in 14:22–24 is not supplied. Struck replaces smote without adding that all those struck were killed.
15: God’s address to Abram is singular and uses you/your. Abram’s direct petitions retain Thou and the accompanying wilt/hast in 15:2–3. Ordinary narrative now uses to, here, how and direct word order where the earlier archaism impeded speech.

I shield you in 15:1 remains a verb. The difficult Masek and Damascus Eliezer construction in 15:2 is retained for specialist review. Seed remains in 15:3–5, 13 and 18. The repeated from you in 15:4, repeated three years old in 15:9, the passive reckoning in 15:6, and the four hundred years and fourth generation remain.

Abram sat down with them in 15:11, trance in 15:12, the smoking furnace and plural torches in 15:17, and the future land grant in 15:18 are retained from the consulted Greek. Their interpretation has not been settled through an apparatus comparison. The three actions enslave, afflict and humble in 15:13 and all the named peoples in 15:19–21 remain.
16: Sara continues the accepted Genesis 11 name spelling. In 16:2 you may have children addresses Abram in the singular. The first-person when I saw in 16:5 remains Sara’s speech. These grammatical relationships have not been recast into familiar wording from another tradition.

Hands, bosom and face are retained where they carry the passage’s images and relationships. Slave woman, afflicted and humble yourself remain explicit. Wild man and the plural hands in 16:12 are retained. Too numerous to count in 16:10 expresses the stated multitude without giving a number.

Hagar directly addresses God as Thou in 16:13. In God who has looked upon me, who refers to God in the relative clause; has is ordinary English third-person agreement, while Thou art retains the direct-address convention. The seeing clauses and translated well name in 16:13–14 remain difficult and require specialist review; no destination, motive or doctrinal explanation has been added.
17: God addresses Abraham with you/your; Abraham’s direct address to God retains Thee in 17:18. Greek number remains significant: in 17:10 the first you shall keep is singular, the following between Me and you is plural, your seed after you is singular, and among you is plural. Verse 11 is plural. In 17:12 among you and your generations are plural, but your house and your seed are singular. In 17:13 your house is singular and your flesh is plural.

Sara becomes Sarah in 17:15, continuing the accepted Genesis 11 spelling while distinguishing the Greek names Sara and Sarra at the naming event. This supersedes the earlier note’s Sarai convention; other names and all ages remain unchanged.

The repeated exceedingly, exceedingly in 17:6, covenant language, eighth-day qualification in 17:14, the change from her to him after the promised child in 17:16, twelve nations in 17:20, and the repeated that very day in 17:23 and 26 are retained. No princes, Almighty, or omitted eighth-day reading has been imported from another tradition. Historical slave status and circumcision language remain explicit.
18: The guest address in 18:3 is singular; the address in 18:4–5 is plural. Ordinary you/your leaves the guest’s identification open, as the earlier lower-case thee did. The narrator explicitly identifies the Lord in 18:13. The singular he said in 18:9 is retained. Clear direct petitions to God in 18:23–32 use Thou/Thee and appropriate verbs.

The oak, feet, tree, bread, milk, curds, advanced in days and way of women imagery is retained. Verse 12 keeps Sarah’s distinct Greek wording; verse 14 retains word rather than replacing it with thing. I knew in 18:19 remains past, and household expresses the people of the house. What I am doing in 18:17 brings out the present activity without adding a plan or motive.

Are being brought to an end in 18:21 is retained as a provisional interpretation of a difficult middle/passive verb. Its relationship to the outcry needs independent review. The intercession preserves fifty, forty-five, forty, thirty, twenty and ten; the repeated By no means and I will surely not destroy; and earth and ashes. No divine anger is inserted into the elliptical petitions of 18:30 and 32.
